scope:
Reviewed: agent loop (src/agent.py, src/main.py), Kubernetes deployment and RBAC (k8s/deployment.yaml, k8s/rbac.yaml), tool dispatch (src/tools/registry.py, src/tools/shell.py, src/tools/git.py), audit logging (src/audit.py), sub-agent spawning (src/subagents.py), configuration (config/agent.yaml), system prompt (prompts/system.md), Dockerfile. Not reviewed: runtime execution, live permission verification, actual Slack/AWS integration behavior. Reviewed the ops-agent codebase: Python agent that runs kubectl, helm, and git commands.
Examined: src/agent.py, src/tools/registry.py, src/tools/shell.py, src/tools/git.py, src/subagents.py, 
config/agent.yaml, Dockerfile, k8s/deployment.yaml, k8s/rbac.yaml, k8s/networkpolicy.yaml, 
k8s/kyverno-verify-images.yaml, prompts/system.md, .github/CODEOWNERS.
Not reviewed: CI workflows (.github/workflows/), GitHub branch protection rules (not visible in repo),
deployment.yaml file location, production runtime evidence. Reviewed configuration and deployment files for ops-agent Slack-based DevOps assistant. Examined config/agent.yaml, k8s/deployment.yaml, k8s/rbac.yaml, k8s/networkpolicy.yaml, Dockerfile, requirements.txt, prompts/system.md, .github/CODEOWNERS, and source files (agent.py, audit.py). No release manifest, ML-BOM, SBOM, rollback procedures, drift detection, release gates, or comprehensive tracing found. Image verification policy via Kyverno and dependency pinning via requirements.txt with hashes present. Reviewed: agent.py (tool loop), tools/ (kubectl, helm, git, registry), subagents.py (worker spawning), audit.py (logging), checkpoint.py (state save/restore), config/agent.yaml (tool allowlist), k8s/ (deployment, RBAC, network policy, image verification), Dockerfile (dependency pinning), prompts/system.md (agent rules). Not reviewed: CI/CD workflows (no .github/workflows/ found), E12 incident runbooks (not in repo), runtime behavior and production deployment. Reviewed: main agent loop (src/agent.py), tool dispatch and shell execution (src/tools/), audit logging (src/audit.py), checkpoint/recovery (src/checkpoint.py), subagent spawning (src/subagents.py), and Kubernetes deployment config (k8s/). Not reviewed: GitHub Actions workflows, Slack integration internals, or production monitoring outside this repo.

findings.title: Minimal tool surface

evidence.note: TOOLS dict has exactly 4 tools: kubectl, helm, git, spawn_worker

checks.check: Each agent role has one explicit allowlist of tool names, with no wildcard grants such as `*`, `mcp__*`, `Bash(*)`, or `bypassPermissions`.
checks.note: TOOLS dict explicitly lists 4 tools with no wildcards; passed to model as TOOL_SCHEMAS

checks.check: Tools discovered from MCP servers are filtered against that allowlist before the model can see or call them.
checks.note: Model receives TOOL_SCHEMAS (static list), not discovered tools; no MCP servers

checks.check: The dispatcher rejects a call to any tool name not on the allowlist, instead of looking it up dynamically.
checks.quote: def dispatch(name: str, arguments: dict, run_id: str) -> str:
checks.note: dispatch() checks 'if name not in TOOLS' before executing any tool

checks.check: Allow and approval decisions never read server-supplied hints or descriptions such as `readOnlyHint` or 'read-only'.
checks.quote: """The only tools the model can call. Unknown tool names are refused."""
checks.note: No MCP servers; no server hints used in dispatch logic; only explicit TOOLS dict used

checks.check: File access is limited to named directories, not the whole filesystem.
checks.note: git tool restricts file access to /work directory; kubectl/helm access cluster resources only

findings.summary: Tool surface is minimal with explicit allowlist (4 tools), static dispatch, and directory-scoped file access.
findings.next_step: Confirm at runtime that dispatch() rejects a tool name not in TOOLS dict and verify that no other code paths bypass the tool registry.

findings.title: Destructive-action interception

evidence.note: Destructive kubectl verbs (delete, apply) in allowlist without per-operation approval

checks.check: High-impact operations are listed in code or config and blocked by default, including deletes, destructive updates, force-pushes, infrastructure teardown, payment changes, outbound sends, and deleting audit records or changing their retention.
checks.quote: kubectl_verbs: [get, describe, logs, top, rollout, scale, delete, apply, annotate]
checks.note: delete and apply (destructive) are in the allowed list; they run without approval gate. No audit of deletions or audit-log retention policy found.

checks.check: The gate runs in the execution path when the call runs and checks the operation, the target, and the arguments, not only a tool name, command name, or blocklist of words.
checks.note: Gate only checks the verb name (first word), not the operation target or arguments. 'kubectl delete pod important-thing' passes the gate.

checks.check: The same gate covers every path that can do the operation, including raw shell, HTTP or API clients, other tools, and requests to a more powerful tool or peer agent.
checks.quote: def helm(args: str, context: str) -> str:\n    return _run(f'helm --kube-context {context} {args}')
checks.note: helm() has no gate at all; can run 'helm delete' or any destructive command. git can push/force-push from allowed-subcommands list.

checks.check: A blocked operation runs only after approval from a person or system with higher authority than the agent; a prompt, comment, or model instruction is never the enforcement.
checks.quote: No approval check found in agent loop
checks.note: No approval mechanism; agent runs all allowed commands immediately without human review

checks.check: For an agent that reads untrusted input, reaches sensitive data or systems, and acts outside, every consequential action is gated, unless code shows untrusted content cannot pick the tool, destination, or arguments (for example plan-then-execute or capability tracking).
checks.quote: @app.command('/ops')\ndef handle_ops(ack, command, respond):\n    summary = run(goal=command['text'], requester=command['user_id'])
checks.note: Agent reads goal from Slack command text (untrusted input), has kubectl/helm/git access (sensitive), and applies changes (outside action). All three capabilities present but consequential actions not individually gated.

red_flags_found: config/agent.yaml:14 kubectl delete and apply allowed without approval gate
src/tools/shell.py:23 helm() runs any helm command with no verb checks
src/tools/shell.py:12 subprocess.run with shell=True allows command injection
prompts/system.md:8 force-push allowed without approval mechanism
src/tools/git.py:23 subprocess.run(['git', ...]) but args from model are split() without sanitization
findings.summary: Destructive kubectl operations (delete, apply) are in allowlist but not individually gated; helm has no verb checks at all; git force-push allowed without approval. Operations flow directly to subprocess with minimal validation.
findings.next_step: Implement per-operation approval gate before executing destructive actions. Require approval for: kubectl delete/apply, helm upgrade/delete, git push/force-push. Check operation args, not just verb names. Block helm/git command injection.
